names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιος Ιωνάς ο θαυματουργός Αρχιεπίσκοπος Νοβογορδίας», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 5 ноября ст. ст., «Святитель Иона, архиепископ Новгородский», with the rank words left off. The line itself gives the name in the genitive.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 5. новембар ст. ст., „Св. Јона архиепископ Новгородски.“ — «Св.» is "saint" and not a rank, «архиепископ» is the `archbishop` grade `types` keeps, and «Новгородски» is the complement of «архиепископ», the see it governs, so it comes off with the rank: the same reading as «еп. Патавски», «еп. Наесонски» and «еп. Мирски» on the three days before this one, and as `andrew-of-crete`’s «архиеп. Критски». The see is already in this folder’s `office`. `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the bare string as held by `jonah-of-moscow`, `jonah-the-prophet` and `jonah-the-sabaite`, so this form makes the fold four wide and the key is in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`. His baptismal name «Иванушка», which the entry prints inside another man’s reported speech and in a diminutive, is NOT stored: it is not the form the book names him by.

death.note: Both of his life pages give the day and the year — «Архиепископ Иона почил о Господе 5 ноября 1470 г.» and «5 ноября 1470 года, причастившись Святых Таин, святитель отошел ко Господу» — and the calendar's line for 5 ноября ст. ст. ends «(1470)». saint.gr had given the folder the same year from its head line, «(; - 1470)», as traditional; it is now attested by two further pages that print the day as well.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 ноября ст. ст. — «Свт. Ионы , архиеп. Новгородского (1470).»

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιος Ιωνάς ο θαυματουργός Αρχιεπίσκοπος Νοβογορδίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. A Russian saint on the Greek calendar: his own church reckons in the Julian calendar and that row is left undocumented here, because days.pravoslavie.ru was not read for him.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.11.2025 (5. новембар ст. ст.) — „Св. Јона архиепископ Новгородски.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, one man, eleven sentences. Quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. `types` and `office` UNTOUCHED and the heading confirms both: «архиепископ» is the `archbishop` and «Новгородски» the see already in `office` as Archbishop of Novgorod; `wonderworker` is this folder’s own and the entry’s last two sentences are exactly that. **`dates` UNTOUCHED AT 1470, AND THIS BOOK PRINTS 1570 — A CENTURY LATER.** «Упокоји се мирно 5. нов. 1570. године» against days.pravoslavie.ru’s two life pages, which give «Архиепископ Иона почил о Господе 5 ноября 1470 г.» and agree with one another; the DAY is the same in both books and only the century differs, the folder’s basis is `attested`, and the gate refuses an `attested` interval spanning more than a century. AND THE ENTRY CONTRADICTS ITS OWN YEAR IN ITS OWN SENTENCES: it has him prophesied over as a boy by «Михаил, јуродиви Клопски», who is `michael-of-klops` and whom this corpus dates to the fifteenth century, and chosen «по смрти архиеп. Јевтимија», after the death of `euthymius-of-novgorod`, likewise fifteenth — so 1570 cannot stand beside the people the same entry puts around him. SO NOTHING WAS WIDENED AND NOTHING WAS CORRECTED IN THE DATA: the year is recorded here and in the life as what this book prints, and 1470 stands. AUTHOR: this is the first figure in this block that reads as a slip in the source rather than as a disagreement between sources, and the handling taken — record, do not widen, do not repair — is a reading of mine and not a rule I was given. NO `related` ROW ADDED AND FOUR PEOPLE ARE NAMED. `michael-of-klops` and `euthymius-of-novgorod` are both `related` here IN BOTH DIRECTIONS already, so a third book confirms both. The see of Metropolitan of Moscow he was offered and refused pleading old age is the see of `jonah-of-moscow`, also `related` here already, and the entry does not name that man. And the God-fearing widow who took him in as an orphan and raised him is unnamed. NO `locations`: Novgorod and Moscow are named and the folder has never held the key. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: he was born in Novgorod and left an orphan early; a God-fearing widow took and raised him; Michael the fool-for-Christ of Klops, seeing him as a boy, said to him prophetically „Иванушка, учи се приљежно, јер ћеш бити архиепископ у овоме великом Новгороду“ — Ivanushka, study diligently, for you will be archbishop in this great Novgorod — WHICH ALSO GIVES HIS BAPTISMAL NAME, Иван, in a diminutive and in another man’s mouth; he was pious and merciful AS FEW MORTAL MEN ARE; he raised churches and monasteries; he refused the see of Moscow for his old age; and A HUNDRED YEARS AFTER HIS DEATH THERE WAS A GREAT FIRE IN NOVGOROD IN WHICH HIS RELICS DID NOT BURN, but afterwards began to show a healing power and to give off a wonderful fragrance. THE BAPTISMAL NAME IS NOT STORED AS A NAME FORM: it is printed inside reported speech and in a diminutive, which is neither the form the book names him by nor a form it prints of its own account. THE FOLD: `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the bare «Јона» as held by `jonah-of-moscow`, `jonah-the-prophet` and `jonah-the-sabaite`, so this form makes a FOUR-member fold where the string had three holders and no key; the key is in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Исправление веры, и образ кротости,/ и якоже сад посреде рая,/ преподобными делы твоими мир просвещаеши,/ и сего ради к мощем твоим любовию прикасаемся и верно вопием:/ предстани в помощь воспевающим/ память твою светоносную, отче Ионо,// и моли спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 ноября ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителя Ионы»

english.text: A rule of faith and an image of meekness, and like a garden in the midst of paradise, thou dost enlighten the world by thy holy deeds; and therefore we touch thy relics with love and cry out in faith: stand forth to help those who hymn thy light-bearing memory, O father Jonah, and pray that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Свыше приял еси Божественную благодать/ ходатайствовати Богу и человеком,/ яко архиерей возношение вознося,/ и мир людем твоим снося,/ и обилие плодов, Ионо блаженне,/ ты бо еси Великаго Новаграда похвала// и сущих о нем радость.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 ноября ст. ст. — «Кондак святителя Ионы»

english.text: From on high thou didst receive divine grace to be a mediator with God for men, offering up the oblation as a hierarch and bringing down peace upon thy people and an abundance of fruits, O blessed Jonah; for thou art the boast of Great Novgorod and the joy of all that is about her.
